newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers start annual farm price marathon.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers start annual farm price marathon.

text.p: European Union agriculture ministers started marathon talks on Monday to fix farm prices for the coming year amidst strong opposition to plans to cut aid to wealthy wheat farmers.

All countries except Britain and Sweden fiercely oppose a proposal by Farm Commissioner Franz Fishler to cut payments to cereals and oilseed farmers by 1.4 billion Ecus ($1.6 billion) to help fund aid for beef producers hit by the mad cow crisis.
"We are rigorously against it," German Farm Minister Jochen Borchert told reporters before the meeting started. "We expect a majority to vote against the proposal."
Other ministers also attacked the proposal.

"Spain is totally opposed," Spanish Farm Minister Loyola De Palacio told Reuters, explaining the proposed reduction constituted a major change in EU farm policy and could not be tacked onto the annual farm price package.
"We are anxious to resist the arable aid cuts," added Irish Farm Minister Ivan Yates, noting that the price of animal feed grain had fallen since 1995.
But British Farm Minister Jack Cunningham backed Fischler.
"I hope to see support for reductions in cereals aid," he told Reuters before the meeting. "There is ample evidence that there has been over-compensation for cereals."

The Commission has estimated cereals farmers were overpaid by 8.5 billion Ecus ($9.6 billion) during the past four marketing years. A British study put the excess much higher at 14.3 billion Ecus ($16.2 billion).
The payments were intended to compensate farmers for cuts in support prices agreed under 1992 farm reforms to remove grain, beef and dairy surpluses and to curb costs.
Since then cereals market prices have soared but farmers have still been paid for losses they never suffered.
